title: Structured Denoising Diffusion Models in Discrete State-Spaces

nodes.text: Discrete Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (D3PMs) are diffusion-like generative models for discrete data whose forward corruption is defined by Markov transition matrices Qt over categorical variables, with q(xt|xt-1) = Cat(xt; p = xt-1 Qt).
nodes.evidence: we introduce Discrete Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (D3PMs), diffusionlike generative models for discrete data

nodes.text: D3PMs generalize the multinomial diffusion model of Hoogeboom et al. by going beyond corruption processes with uniform transition probabilities to a broad family of structured transition matrices.
nodes.evidence: diffusionlike generative models for discrete data that generalize the multinomial diffusion model of Hoogeboom et al. [20], by going beyond corruption processes with uniform transition probabilities.

nodes.text: Several structured transition matrices are introduced: uniform, absorbing-state ([MASK]), discretized Gaussian (mimicking continuous-space Gaussian kernels for ordinal data), and token-embedding-distance matrices that transition more frequently between semantically similar tokens.
nodes.evidence: matrices that mimic Gaussian kernels in continuous space, matrices based on nearest neighbors in embedding space, and matrices that introduce absorbing states.

nodes.text: BERT is a one-step diffusion model: a D3PM forward step that replaces ~10% of tokens with [MASK] and ~5% uniformly at random yields exactly the BERT denoising objective.
nodes.evidence: BERT is a one-step diffusion model ... this leads precisely to the BERT denoising objective, i.e. Lvb - LT = -Eq(x1|x0)[log p(x0|x1)] = LBERT

nodes.text: Autoregressive models are a special case of discrete diffusion: a deterministic forward process that masks tokens one-by-one in order makes the D3PM reverse process equivalent to autoregressive generation.
nodes.evidence: Autoregressive models are (discrete) diffusion models: Consider a diffusion process that deterministically masks tokens one-by-one

nodes.text: The absorbing-state ([MASK]) transition matrix lets D3PMs draw a connection between diffusion models and autoregressive and mask-based generative models, with a stationary distribution placing all mass on the [MASK] token.
nodes.evidence: The third allows us to draw a connection between diffusion models and autoregressive and mask-based generative models.

nodes.text: An x0-parameterization of the reverse process predicts logits of p(x0|xt) and combines them with q(xt-1|xt,x0), automatically enforcing the correct sparsity pattern dictated by Qt and enabling inference k steps at a time.
nodes.evidence: pθ(xt-1|xt) ∝ sum q(xt-1, xt|x0) p(x0|xt) ... automatically ensures that the learned reverse probability distribution pθ(xt-1|xt) has the correct sparsity pattern

nodes.text: A new loss combines the variational lower bound with an auxiliary cross-entropy denoising term, L_lambda = Lvb + lambda E[-log p(x0|xt)], which stabilizes training and improves image sample quality.
nodes.evidence: we introduce a new auxiliary denoising objective ... Lλ = Lvb + λ Eq(x0)Eq(xt|x0)[− log p(x0|xt)].

nodes.text: A noise schedule based on linearly interpolating the mutual information I(xt;x0) toward zero is proposed; for absorbing-state D3PMs it reduces exactly to the (T-t+1)^-1 schedule of Sohl-Dickstein et al.
nodes.evidence: linearly interpolating the mutual information between xt and x0 to zero ... this schedule reduces to exactly the (T - t + 1)^-1 schedule proposed by Sohl-Dickstein et al.

nodes.text: Unlike continuous diffusion (which has focused almost exclusively on additive Gaussian noise), the D3PM framework lets the choice of transition matrix embed domain knowledge, and this choice is an important design decision that improves results.
nodes.evidence: the choice of transition matrix is an important design decision that leads to improved results in image and text domains.

nodes.text: On CIFAR-10, D3PM models approach the sample quality of and exceed the log-likelihood of the continuous-space DDPM model of Ho et al.
nodes.evidence: our models approach the sample quality and exceed the log-likelihood of the continuous-space DDPM model.

nodes.text: For text, D3PMs strongly outperform non-autoregressive baselines on character-level text generation and scale to large vocabularies and long sequences on LM1B.
nodes.evidence: this model class achieves strong results on character-level text generation while scaling to large vocabularies on LM1B.
